learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the psychological pain of physical impairment, the feeling of alienation, and how a change in perspective can bring hope and positivity to life.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derry is a 14-year-old boy whose face is half-burnt by acid. He is deeply bitter, withdrawn, and hates being around people because they either pity him, stare in horror, or call him a 'terrible thing'.
Mr. Lamb is an old man who lost his leg in a war and has a tin leg. Kids mockingly call him 'Lamey-Lamb', but he doesn't mind. He keeps his gates open, makes jelly from crab apples, and loves life.

Mr. Lamb teaches Derry about perspective. He looks at his garden and says a weed and a flower are both green, growing life. It's only human perception that makes one a 'flower' and the other a 'weed'.
Through a long conversation, Mr. Lamb convinces Derry that his burned face doesn't define him. What matters is inside (what he thinks and feels). He shouldn't lock himself away out of fear.

Inspired, Derry runs home to tell his mother he is going back to help Mr. Lamb. Despite her warnings, he returns, only to find that Mr. Lamb has fallen from his ladder and died. But Derry is permanently changed—he is no longer afraid.

fun_activity.title: 🍏 The Crab Apple Jelly
fun_activity.instructions: Mr. Lamb turns sour crab apples into sweet jelly. Think of a 'sour' (bad) experience you had recently. Write down one 'sweet' lesson you learned from it!

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast the two characters: Both are physically impaired, but Derry is severely pessimistic and alienated, while Mr. Lamb is optimistic and socially welcoming.

📌 Explain the 'Beauty and the Beast' reference: Derry believes that unlike the fairy tale, he will never change into a handsome prince, and nobody will ever kiss him (except his mother, on the good side of his face).
📌 The ending signifies the passing of the torch. Mr. Lamb dies physically, but his spirit and positivity live on in the newly transformed Derry.
quick_recap: ⭐ Acid ate Derry's face, but as Derry realizes, his anger and hatred are eating him away from the inside.
⭐ Mr. Lamb keeps his windows without curtains because he doesn't want to shut out the light, the wind, or the world.
⭐ The play deals with the theme that people with physical impairments suffer more from society's insensitive attitude than from the disability itself.
